verdict: NEGATIVE RESULT — formatting augmentation REDUCES distinct-2 on kanto (0.3305 -> 0.2389) and adds zero effective diversity by the repo's own diversity_lib. Reverted per the brief's own rule.

hypothesis.source: EMNLP-2025 (dvlab) formatting augmentation — layout variants add diversity at zero LLM cost and zero fact drift.
hypothesis.prediction: A bounded multiplier of formatting variants on the template floor raises distinct-2 without touching faithfulness.

implementation_as_tested.shape: pure PREFIX transforms only, so the payload survives verbatim and no variant can introduce a hallucinated entity — that is what would have kept the faithfulness gate unaffected by construction
implementation_as_tested.guard: _preserves_payload asserted the original text is a contiguous substring AND every entity_id appears unchanged; 0 variants were skipped as unsafe
implementation_as_tested.suite_while_it_existed: 7/7 (entity survival, contiguous-substring, bounded multiplier, originals-never-dropped, determinism, provenance labelling, zero-fraction no-op)

measurement_on_kanto.estimand: distinct-2 over the generic_expand template floor for pokemon-lore/kanto, same triples throughout
measurement_on_kanto.arithmetic: 715 variants added (x1.4857). Total bigrams rose ~48% while UNIQUE bigrams rose only ~12% (2475 -> 2778). distinct-2 is unique/total, so duplicating a payload behind a new prefix necessarily drives it down.

second_measure.test: diversity_lib.effective_forms on a surface and its indented variant
second_measure.reading: The repo's own diversity library already classifies a prefix variant as the SAME form. So the augmentation adds zero effective diversity while inflating the surface count — it would spend exposure budget on rows the pipeline does not count as distinct.

why_the_negative_result_is_structural: Guaranteeing zero fact drift forced prefix-only transforms (anything editing inside the string risks corrupting an entity, which the faithfulness gate exists to prevent). But a prefix-only variant is, by construction, a near-duplicate: identical token sequence, one extra leading token. distinct-n is a ratio and SemDeDup's jaccard is a set overlap, so both metrics are structurally unable to reward this shape. The dvlab result may still hold for robustness measures this repo does not compute; it does not hold for the diversity gate the brief named as the ruler.

decision.rule_applied: the brief's own — 'If an item's ablation regresses, revert it and report the negative result with the arithmetic — a proven no is a result.'
decision.why_not_kept_behind_a_flag: Dead code that measured worse is the same failure as the h7b inert budget: it would advertise that formatting augmentation is available and beneficial when the one metric this repo gates on says otherwise.

if_revisited: Pick a metric the mechanism can actually move: token-level robustness / eval under formatting shift, not distinct-n or jaccard.

Or use interior transforms (space insertion, markdown emphasis around non-entity spans) with an entity-span mask so the payload changes without touching entities — strictly more machinery than a prefix, and it needs the faithfulness gate re-proven.
Either way it should be measured against install strength on pinned probes, not against a diversity ratio that penalises duplicated payloads by construction.
deviations: The item was implemented in full, with a passing 7-case suite, before the measurement condemned it. The suite was deleted with the code rather than left orphaned.
Only the distinct-2 measure the brief named was used as the ruler; no alternative metric was substituted after the fact to rescue the result.
P0's balance change is unaffected and stays landed — the balanced floor is where distinct-2 actually improved (0.2722 -> 0.3305).

gates.note: generic_expand carries no residual reference to the reverted mechanism (grep-verified 0).
